title: Timeboxing work in turns
when: A task could grow without end (research, polish, debugging) and the plan must cap it with a budget and a stop rule.
prompt:
Goal: Each open ended task has a turn budget, a minimum deliverable and a rule for what happens when the budget runs out.
Steps:
1. Identify open ended tasks: polish, investigate, optimize, explore options.
2. Give each a budget in turns (for example 4) and say it in the detail.
3. Define the minimum deliverable that must exist when the budget ends: a note with findings, a patch, a list of options.
4. Define checkpoints: at half the budget, the worker writes a note with what it found so far.
5. Define the stop rule: when the budget ends, finish with what exists and call done with a summary of what is left.
6. Give leftover work to a later task or the user notes, never extend silently.
Quality bar:
- Budgets are numbers.
- The minimum deliverable is concrete.
- Stopping on time still leaves something useful.
Pitfalls:
- A polish task with no end.
- Budgets so small that nothing useful can exist.
- Ending with nothing written because the task was not done.
Verify:
- [ ] Open ended tasks have budgets.
- [ ] Each has a minimum deliverable.
- [ ] A halfway note is planned.
- [ ] Leftovers have a home.
Output: Task details with "Budget: N turns. Minimum: ... When out of turns: ..." lines.

examples.input: investigate why the page feels slow
examples.output: Budget 5 turns; minimum: note with the three biggest causes and one patch; then done
